title: company-ops-orbit-sprint-commitments-v0-1
summary: Working notes from the company ops "orbit" sprint workshop — consolidates OKR candidates, draft exec update bullets, proposed all-hands narrative, and a short decision log. Intentionally rough: prioritization trade-offs and unanswered questions highlighted for leadership review.
body:
Context:
This doc captures the output of the cross-functional 'Orbit' sprint workshop on 2024-07-18 and follow-up syncs. Goal: produce a minimal set of company commitments for the next 90 days that can be translated into team-level OKRs and an all-hands narrative.

Why "Orbit"? We used the metaphor to emphasize a tight cadence: commit -> measure -> course-correct within one orbit (~90 days). The language below is intentionally blunt: we need commitments that align to our production-first inference thesis (latency, cost, deployment flexibility).

High-level constraints we agreed on (reminder):
- Prioritize customer SLAs and reliability improvements that unlock Dedicated deals this quarter.
- Preserve velocity for Redwood Optimize feature work (cost tooling) but pare scope where it increases infra fragility.
- Reserve a small allocation of research cycles (applied ML) for model quantization/inference breakthroughs that materially reduce TCO.

Executive update draft bullets (short):
- Performance & Reliability: Rolled out 2 regional fallbacks and reduced tail-latency P95 by ~12% on average across production models; next step is a canary window for Dedicated customers.
- Commercial momentum: Several mid-market pilots converted to Dedicated trials; pipeline improving but conversion time remains a blocker.
- Product & Cost: Redwood Optimize limited beta shows promising analyst-level unit-cost reductions; need to expand sample set for stronger claims.

OKR candidates (90-day orbit) — raw draft (to be converted into final OKRs):
1) Reliability Commitment (owner: Lena Ortiz)
- Objective: Make inference predictable for Dedicated customers.
- Key results (draft): reduce production P95 latency by 15% for committed models; achieve 99.9% uptime for Dedicated pools; run four disaster-recovery drills across two regions.

2) Cost/Performance Toolkit (owner: Jonah Greene)
- Objective: Ship Optimize v1 plus quantization playbook for common workloads.
- Key results (draft): deliver Optimize UI + API 1.0; validate quantization recommendations on 5 high-volume customer workloads; lower average per-token cost by 8% on benchmark workload set.

3) Developer Adoption & Enablement (owner: Marcus Patel)
- Objective: Reduce onboarding time and increase self-serve launches.
- Key results (draft): shrink average time-to-first-call by 40%; add three starter templates for common patterns (chat, reranking, embeddings); host two community office hours.

4) Private & Compliance Readiness (owner: Asha Rao)
- Objective: Remove blockers for two enterprise pilots to go Private.
- Key results (draft): complete SOC-like audit checklist for Private; deliver an on-prem deployment runbook and a tested KMS integration for two customers.

Notes on OKR candidates: these are intentionally coarse. We need numerical baselines (e.g., current P95 numbers, cost per token) before locking KRs. Action item: product-ops to send baseline spreadsheet by 2024-07-22.

All-hands narrative (outline):
- Theme: "Predictable Inference, Practical Economics" — why it matters; short human stories from a customer pilot that nearly missed SLA pre-fixes.
- What we shipped recently: top 3 wins (latency work, Dedicated onboarding, Optimize beta).
- What we commit to this orbit: the four high-level commitments above (reliability, cost toolkit, developer adoption, private readiness).
- How each team will measure success: quick bullets per team so everyone has a visible signal post/all-hands.
- Close: where we need help (crowdsourcing playbooks, polishing demos, writing customer stories).

Comms plan (brief):
- Pre-all-hands (T-minus 7 days): exec email + one-pager to managers with talking points; slideshow draft due 2024-08-01.
- All-hands (T-minus 0): 20-min exec update, 10-min demo (Optimize), 15-min AMA panel with eng/product leads.
- Post-all-hands (T-plus 1 day): publish one-pager and recording; push OKR assignments into team trackers; open a follow-up thread in #company-all for clarifying questions.

Decision log (workshop decisions):
- Use the 90-day "orbit" unit for company commitments instead of a quarter boundary for this year — rationale: faster feedback loop.
- Prioritize reliability and customer SLA work over feature expansion for hosted API this orbit.
- Approve an internal freeze on non-critical infra changes during the first 3 weeks of the rollout window.

Open questions / risks (explicit):
- Do we have reliable baselines for per-token cost across supported models? (ACTION: infra finance to surface by 2024-07-22).
- Dedicated commercial conversion timeline uncertain — if conversion lag persists, do we shift more engineering to conversion-critical bugs?
- All-hands cadence: if we adopt the orbit cadence permanently, need to rejigger our tracking tools (Linear/Jira tags + reporting).

Quick workshop notes & sticky points (raw):
- Many teams asked for more prescriptive rollout playbooks for canary failures — product-ops to draft a first-pass.
- SRE highlighted a recurring DB failover pattern correlated with long KV cache warms; possible mitigation: staggered cache prefetch per pod.
- Sales wants clearer milestone language for Dedicated SLAs to present in contract pilots (KR -> milestone mapping).

Immediate action items (owners and target dates):
- Product-ops: baseline spreadsheet (metrics for KRs) — due 2024-07-22 (owner: Priya).
- Eng-serving-runtime: P95 baseline and tail-latency investigation summary — due 2024-07-25 (owner: Lena).
- Applied-ML: quantization test plan and required customer workloads list — due 2024-07-29 (owner: Jonah).
- Comms: slides + exec talking points draft — due 2024-08-01 (owner: Marcus).

Notes to leadership (brief and informal):
- We deliberately kept the OKR set small (4 focuses) to avoid signal dilution. Please flag if you want an additional cross-company priority (e.g., international/regional expansion) included — we can slot it but will recommend deprioritizing one of the four above.
- This doc will be the source-of-truth for the orbit kickoff; please add comments inline or ping me for a short sync slot.

Appendix (links & references):
- Benchmark spreadsheet (placeholder): jira:OPS-512 -> attachments
- Previous midyear notes: confluence:midyear-alignment-2024
- Sample Dedicated contract language: github:contracts/dedicated-template.md

End of notes.

Freeze non-critical infra changes for first 3 weeks of rollout
